"""Days that are nothing like a normal day: storms, holidays, one-off closures.

Every other module treats one day the same as the next, so a snowstorm or a
holiday just looks like a strange dip in the numbers. This is the list of
which days those are, so pages can tell them apart later.

The handful below are ones you can spot just by looking at the daily
totals: Christmas, the Fourth of July, Thanksgiving and New Year's Day are
all sharply quieter than the days around them, every year they appear in
the data, and the February 2019 snowstorm is the biggest drop on record.
Ryan has a fuller list in his email; fold those in here too, one line each.
"""

def label_for_month(month):
    """The name of a tracked event day that falls in this calendar month, or None.

    Monthly totals are keyed by the first of the month, not by day, so this
    matches on year and month instead of an exact date.
    """
    names = {name for day, name in EVENT_DAYS.items()
             if day.year == month.year and day.month == month.month}
    return ", ".join(sorted(names)) if names else None

    """Total, average day and busiest day for each calendar year, oldest first.

    Each entry is (year, total, average day, busiest day, busiest day's count).

def yearly_summary(readings):
    """Total, average day and busiest day for each calendar year, oldest first.

    Each entry is (year, total, average day, busiest day, busiest day's count).
    The average leaves out event days (storms, holidays), so one snowbound
    Monday doesn't drag down what an ordinary day looks like. It's otherwise
    over days that are actually in the file, so a partial year at either end
    of the data isn't averaged down over months it doesn't cover. The total
    still counts every day, event days included.
    """
    days_by_year = {}
    for day, count in daily_totals(readings):
        days_by_year.setdefault(day.year, []).append((day, count))
    summary = []
    for year, days in sorted(days_by_year.items()):
        total = sum(count for _, count in days)
        busiest_day, busiest_count = max(days, key=lambda kv: kv[1])
        normal_days = [count for day, count in days if not events.label(day)]
        avg = round(sum(normal_days) / len(normal_days))
        summary.append((year, total, avg, busiest_day, busiest_count))
    return summary
